sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law tradition with Samoan statutes and customary law; unitary national legal system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus)
Tax information exchange arrangements with Australia and New Zealand
Samoa is a member of the WTO and party to the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended), Terrorism Prevention Act 2002 (as amended), Financial Institutions Act 1996, Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Guidelines, and International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) including its statutory registers of members, directors, and beneficial ownership records.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent home-country issuing authority and licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the home-country competent authority or consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate registry extract, certificate of incorporation, and register of directors for any corporate UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney authorizing the licensed Samoa registered agent to incorporate and administer the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of beneficial ownership and source of funds/wealth
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoan notary public or foreign notary with authentication
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Samoa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, shareholders, and agents against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Samoa domestic sanctions list, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and World Bank exclusion lists. PEP status must be identified, risk-rated, approved at senior management level, and subjected to enhanced ongoing monitoring. Independent source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation is required for all enhanced-risk relationships. Screening results and supporting evidence must be retained for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Companies and International Companies Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in Latin/Roman script. Samoan and English names are accepted. Non-Latin names, including Chinese ideograms, must be transliterated/romanized, and the Latin-script name constitutes the official registered name. A certified English or Samoan translation is required for any Chinese-language articles of association. An International Company name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', or an approved abbreviation denoting limited liability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by written request to the Registrar of Companies before expiration. Rejection letters state grounds; an administrative appeal may be filed at MCIL within 14 working days of rejection. The appeal must set out legal and factual grounds and propose two alternative names. The Registrar must decide within 21 working days. A further appeal is available to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour, and judicial review may be sought in the Samoan Supreme Court if the refusal is procedurally unlawful or ultra vires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not acceptable as the sole substantive presence for an ISIC 6619 virtual card issuer. A licensed Samoa registered agent must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa for service of process and regulatory access. Virtual back-office functions may be tolerated only if a Samoan resident AML compliance officer and the licensed agent sustain local commercial substance; a mail-forwarding address without local staff does not satisfy the Central Bank of Samoa's AML/CFT expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a high-risk, license-gated financial services and card-issuing entity, the likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is 65% in the first operating year. For an inactive or unlicensed International Company the likelihood is approximately 10-20%. Central Bank of Samoa and the Financial Intelligence Unit may conduct unannounced on-site examinations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International Company incorporation filing and Certificate of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour — International Companies Registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization bundle for UBO, director, and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, consular posts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent, registered office, and corporate services (first year, prepaid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Samoan registered agent / fiduciary service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Samoa International Companies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, and enhanced due diligence report
Preliminary Central Bank license and regulatory classification assessment for virtual card issuing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal counsel / financial regulatory adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for financial services licensing scoping

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended — ss. 5-6 (incorporation), ss. 20-23 (constitution), s. 42 (registered office), s. 51 (registered agent), ss. 62 and 67 (directors and officers); International Finance Authority Act 2013 (administration by SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (SIFA Form 1) together with the executed Constitution (combined Memorandum and Articles of Association)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account rule under the International Companies Act 1987; at least one issued share is required (s. 21). Share capital may be denominated in any currency. The virtual card issuing special licence remains subject to prudential capitalization conditions imposed by the licensing authority on a case-by-case basis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF ______ (Company), adopted by unanimous written consent of the sole director and shareholder:

1. RESOLVED that the Company adopt its signed Constitution as the governing instrument under the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), and fix the registered office at the offices of the Licensed Registered Agent, Apia, Samoa.

2. RESOLVED that the share subscription be accepted and one ordinary share issued to the founding subscriber for lawful consideration.

3. RESOLVED that ______ be appointed Director and ______ be appointed Secretary of the Company.

4. RESOLVED that management and the Registered Agent are authorized to effect all statutory filings, apply for the virtual card issuing and payment services licenses, open bank settlement accounts, and engage professional advisers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (private practitioner licensed by SIFA) with name index records maintained by the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked proposed names in English or Chinese (Chinese names accompanied by a romanized rendering). The registered agent searches the SIFA company index and rejects names identical to existing companies, names suggesting government patronage, or names that are otherwise prohibited. The approved name is reserved for 30 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese company names (three ranked options)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused on grounds of similarity or prohibited character, file a written appeal with SIFA and select the next alternative name; administrative resubmission fee only if a fresh index search is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of a SIFA-licensed registered agent and AML/KYC onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent licensed under the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a registered agent engagement letter covering the registered office in Samoa, agent consent to act, and corporate secretarial duties. The agent conducts customer due diligence, verifies beneficial ownership, screens against sanctions and watchlists, and opens the client file in accordance with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of each shareholder and director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Curriculum vitae and personal statement for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Supplement incomplete KYC documentation within 7 working days; re-submit notarized or apostilled copies if certification is deficient; the agent re-runs sanctions screening after any correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution, and notarization of the Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent in coordination with legal counsel and a notary public exercising jurisdiction under Samoa law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel drafts the Constitution (combined memorandum and articles) compliant with ss. 20-23 of the International Companies Act 1987, addressing share classes, registered office, objects, director powers, indemnity, and the approved virtual card issuing business scope. The founding subscriber executes the Constitution as a deed; signature pages are notarized before submission to SIFA.
required_dossiers: Subscriber declaration of intention to incorporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries inconsistent provisions, amend the Constitution by supplementary resolution of the subscriber and re-file; purely clerical corrections may be accepted without re-execution at the Registrar's discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory filing and fee payment at the SIFA Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the executed Constitution together with the Application for Incorporation (Form 1), the registered agent's consent, and confirmation of the registered office address in Samoa, against payment of the US$100 government fee. The Registrar verifies statutory compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon satisfaction.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (SIFA Form 1)
AML/KYC file and beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a SIFA requisition or query letter within 14 days with corrective documentation; expedite resolution through the registered agent's correspondence; the filing fee is payable again only if the application is deemed withdrawn and a new application is lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate issuance, officer appointments, and financial licensing filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registrar; Central Bank of Samoa (CBS); Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); Samoa International Finance Authority joint licensing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation and certified constitutive documents from the registered agent; adopt the First Board Resolution; appoint directors and secretary; apply for the virtual card issuing and payment services special licence under the Financial Institutions Act 2015 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; secure office premises and fire safety clearance; open settlement accounts with a licensed commercial bank.
required_dossiers: Payment services special licence application package
Fire safety and premises clearance applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is deferred, address CBS fit-and-proper queries, amend the AML/compliance manual, and resubmit within the statutory window; fire safety deficiencies are cured by corrective works and SFESA re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Licensing Unit, Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting jointly with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for International Company designation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Special Licence for Virtual Card Issuing and Payment Services (High-Risk Financial Services Category) under the Financial Institutions Act 2015 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / General Approval — low-impact commercial office development; Full EIA Report not mandated for this occupancy class
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharge; sanitary wastewater discharged to public sewerage or septic system per Water Resources Regulation; no regulated VOC emissions from office operations; electronic waste (servers, card personalization hardware if any) disposed per Waste Management Regulations; back-up power systems restricted to acoustically insulated zones.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) following premises inspection; structural load and electrical wiring inspection by MCIL-qualified engineers; workplace health and safety registration under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013; occupancy permit from PUMA confirming zoning, means of egress, and occupational capacity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), under the Ministry for Revenue; official filing portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), the IC must first be registered with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). Upon incorporation, apply to the SRA for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using Form TIN-01, attaching the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, and identification of directors/beneficial owners. The SRA issues the TIN within 5 business days. To activate the statutory tax exemption, the IC should obtain a Tax Exemption Certificate for offshore business activities from SIFA, confirming that income derived from sources outside Samoa is exempt from income tax and withholding tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style entity classification election exists in Samoa. The IC is automatically treated as a tax-exempt offshore entity upon fulfilling SIFA compliance requirements. It may elect to be treated as a resident Samoa taxpayer only if it surrenders its IC status and re-domiciles as an ordinary domestic company. Hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS rules are not applicable to exempt ICs, as Samoa maintains no corresponding domestic anti-hybrid provisions for this regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WS$100,000 (annual taxable turnover) for mandatory VAGST registration on any taxable activity, with voluntary registration permitted below this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate currently applies in Samoa. VAGST-registered businesses must issue compliant tax invoices (manual or electronic) containing prescribed details. The SRA operates an online return filing and payment portal, but no continuous transmission to tax authorities is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Samoa and services performed for a non-resident or non-resident-owned IC qualify for zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act 2005 (as amended), provided the supplier retains evidence of export and foreign payment. For an IC supplying virtual card issuing and spend management services exclusively to non-resident clients, the services constitute an exported service and may be zero-rated for VAGST if the IC elects to register; otherwise, the offshore revenue remains outside Samoa's tax net under the IC exemption. Financial and payment processing services supplied to non-residents are eligible for zero-rating where the direct beneficiary is located outside Samoa.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent export zero-rating claims attract criminal prosecution, administrative penalties up to 200% of the evaded tax, and statutory interest on underpaid VAGST. The SRA may retrospectively assess and recover tax within 5 years from the relevant date, which is extended to 10 years for fraudulent activity, contractual, or wilful default. The taxpayer must retain export documentation for 7 years. The IC's tax exemption certificate can be revoked for material non-compliance, exposing the entity to full income tax and VAGST liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) operating under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and the Exchange Control Act 1972, with delegated administrative authority from the Samoa Ministry of Finance for currency, reserve, and cross-border payment oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is fully convertible for current account remittances with CBS General Permission, subject to anti-money laundering documentation. Capital account transfers, including shareholder equity injections and profit repatriation, require a CBS exchange control form (EC2/EC4) and may be subject to a 30-day approval cycle. International Companies (ICs) that adopt the non-resident status of the International Companies Act 1987 are generally ring-fenced from onshore capital controls when transacting exclusively in foreign currency through offshore-designated accounts; however, any conversion into WST or any transaction that affects Samoan residents breaks the ring-fence and triggers full CBS oversight. Profit remittance hurdles include the need for an annual audited financial statement that verifies the company's tax-exempt status and a certificate of clearance from the Samoa Inland Revenue Department.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's Exchange Control Regulations require all service exporters, including offshore ICs providing payment processing and virtual card services, to repatriate export proceeds to a licensed authorized dealer in Samoa within 90 days of the invoice date. CBS General Permission No. 9 waives the mandatory surrender obligation for ICs that maintain a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account, provided the exporter makes a quarterly cash-flow disclosure to the authorized dealer. Where insurance, freight, or card network settlement fee offsets are claimed, the net export proceeds may be repatriated; no fixed statutory conversion ratio (e.g., 25%) applies to ICs, but a domestic licensed service company must convert any WST-denominated revenue within two banking days using the interbank mid-rate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa and cannot act as a primary deposit-taking institution for the local card-issuing treasury. Their permissible use is strictly limited to (i) acquiring merchant card acquirers in the SEPA/UK jurisdiction, (ii) providing an optional expense-control front-end, and (iii) pre-funding the card network sponsor account in non-WST currencies. Any Samoan domestic currency settlement or withdrawal must clear through a licensed Samoan commercial bank; otherwise the IC risks being deemed an unauthorized money service business under the Financial Institutions Act 1996.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2021 and CBS AML/CFT Guidelines mandate enhanced due diligence for 'High_Risk_Special_License' activities. At least one executive director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must be physically present in Apia for an in-person interview at the bank's registered office before account activation. The face-to-face interview may be shortened to a video-confidential call, provided the bank receives an apostilled board resolution, notarized specimen signatures, and a banker's confirmation letter from the remitting foreign bank; however, all major Samoan banks currently require one physical board meeting at the adoption of the corporate treasury resolutions to validate card issuing powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face card distribution with no physical branch footprint and no local Samoan cardholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A proprietary AML/CFT manual aligned with FATF Recommendation 16; the card network BIN sponsorship agreement with Mastercard/Visa detailing merchant onboarding controls; a certified copy of the license issued by an equivalent OECD financial supervisor if operating from a branch in Hong Kong or Singapore; and a monthly transaction-monitoring audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inbound capital large enough to support card float settlement from unrelated IC shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn source-of-wealth affidavits for each contributing shareholder; audited IC financial statements for the last two years; notarized board resolutions authorizing the capital injection; bank letter of reference from the remitting bank; signed deed of irrevocable contribution to the 'Cardholder Settlement Reserve'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to customers in restricted jurisdictions through virtual prepaid cards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A geo-blocking attestation from the card platform provider; a negative-media and sanctions screening report (weaponized using Dow Jones/Refinitiv); a list of merchant acquiring MCC codes that are prohibited; a contractual representation from the BIN sponsor indemnifying the Samoan IC for breach of U.S. OFAC or UN sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border sweep transactions between Samoa and the card network principal clearing bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy document setting per-day and per-month velocity limits; a forensic reconciliation report showing that each sweep corresponds exactly to card purchase authorizations; a flow-of-funds chart demonstrating that no Samoan resident is a card end-user without a valid standalone FX license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection wiring from an offshore IC to the Samoa bank must be via SWIFT MT103 with the following compliance fields: `PURPOSE` code `GIFOR` or `CRED` for equity, and `LOCAL_INSTRUMENT` containing 'WS_IC VC Issuer - Capital Account Top Up'. The IC must file CBS Form EC4 within 14 business days. The beneficiary account must be labelled 'WS_IC Card Fund Escrow' to visibly segregate paid-up capital from operational float. The remitting bank's KYC officer must forward the original instruction via authenticated telex to avoid a duplicate CEMT (Cross-Border Exchange of Information) referral. Funds can be pre-cleared only after submission of the FSA (Samoa Financial Services Authority) registration certificate and the Central Bank's 'Eligible Non-Resident Entity' letter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The dominant clearing rail for virtual card trade settlement is the SWIFT MT103 remittance from the Samoan settlement account to the card network principal clearing bank (JPMorgan Chase, New York or Citibank, London) under the BIN sponsorship agreement, using purpose code `TRIC` (Trade in Services) or `NETT` (Network fee). Payment to non-network trade suppliers may additionally use a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) if the supplier requires documentary credit; however, the default operation is a straight MT103 without LC documentation. Every outbound disbursement must reference the underlying card transaction ID in field 70 of the MT103, and a daily EOD file must be transmitted to the CBS statistical unit for balance-of-payments coding.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla WST/USD spot and outright forwards up to 12 months executed through an authorized dealer, subject to the bank having a valid CBS general permission for hedging non-trade exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD for the offshore liquidity reserve, transacted through an international primary dealer and physically settled in USD or AUD, with both legs reported to the CBS on Form EC5.

Cross-currency swap (FX swap) to convert an AUD-denominated card float into USD at the settlement bank's non-resident desk, permitted if the counterparty is a recognized money-centre bank and the transaction is for liquidity smoothing and not proprietary speculation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Office (Registrar of International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of incorporation; subject to the prescribed filing period under the International Companies Act 1987
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 50 per month or part thereof; continued non-filing for three consecutive months may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the International Company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation Statement of Directors and Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Office (Registrar of International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Annual Return on the anniversary date of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of USD 20 per day for late confirmation filings; Registrar may initiate compulsory deregistration proceedings after notice and continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business License Renewal Confirmation (where applicable for regulated card issuing activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Office and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the expiry date of the license; usually 31 December of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic lapse of license with immediate cessation of virtual card issuing activity; late renewal penalty of USD 100; continued unlicensed operation subject to civil fines and license revocation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the International Company's tax-exempt status review period; generally no later than 30 April of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of tax-exempt status; retroactive corporate income tax assessment at the standard rate; late filing penalties of up to USD 200 and monthly interest accrual on any assessed tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An International Company maintaining a tax-exempt status is generally exempt from a compulsory statutory audit unless it holds a specialized financial services license, undertakes regulated payment or card issuing activity, or is directed by the Registrar to produce audited financial statements; the virtual card issuer business scope triggers mandatory annual audited financial statements by a registered Samoa auditor or a licensed foreign auditor approved by the Central Bank of Samoa
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Samoa; Local GAAP is not separately applicable to International Companies that prepare audited accounts for financial services regulators

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every share transfer in an International Company must be recorded in the Register of Members; an annual confirmation reconciliation of the Beneficial Ownership Register is required to be filed with the International Companies Office, and any change to ultimate beneficial ownership arising from transfers must be updated within 14 days of the transaction; the annual return must confirm that the UBO information continues to reflect the registered members as at the anniversary date

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory zero-rate tax shield for International Companies: under the International Companies Act 1987, s.199, a fully registered Samoa International Company (IC) is exempt from income tax, withholding tax, stamp duty, and exchange control on all income, dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains, whether Samoan-source or foreign-source, provided it does not carry on business with Samoan residents and does not hold Samoan land or a Samoan vessel/aircraft. This operates as a permanent full exemption, not a time-limited tax holiday, producing a 0% effective corporate tax rate for the IC card-issuing vehicle.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Revenue Corporation (SRC) Company Income Tax Return (Form IR-CO), lodged via the SRC Online Services portal at https://www.src.gov.ws/etax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and full settlement due within six months after the end of the company's accounting period; where SRC grants an extension, no later than the 15th day of the seventh month. Provisional tax instalments, when applicable, are due quarterly on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September, and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity status declaration: confirm the company is registered as an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 and remains outside the Samoan domestic tax net.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'Yes' to claim the statutory exemption. Any company carrying on trade with Samoa residents cannot use this box and must file as a domestic taxpayer at 27%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross turnover (in WST) from card issuing, interchange, scheme fees, and spend-management services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter '0' for the exempt IC. Foreign-source card issuing fees are outside the Samoan tax net and must not be voluntarily declared as taxable turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income after exemptions and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter '0'. Attach the International Company tax exemption certificate and a board resolution confirming derivation of no Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and headline tax at 27%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter '0'. Do not claim foreign tax credits in this box because the exempt IC is not within the Samoan corporate tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and endorsement by the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The form must be signed in Samoa by the licensed registered agent. Remote e-signature is not accepted, and a foreign corporate services provider cannot endorse the declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 500 immediately assessed plus WST 50 per day of continuing default; late payment interest of 1.5% per month on unpaid tax; a default exceeding six months permits the SRC to issue a best-of-judgment assessment and revoke the IC tax exemption certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return and Declaration of Compliance, filed with the Samoa Registrar of Companies through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Electronic Services Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months of the date of incorporation and each anniversary thereafter; the licensed registered agent must lodge the return and pay the annual government tariff of approximately WST 400.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office and registered agent must be physically present and licensed in Samoa; a foreign corporate services provider's post-office box is not acceptable.
At least one natural person must be a director; foreign-resident directors are permitted, but economic substance rules require documented board decision-making occurring in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders and location of the share register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The share register need not be physically kept in Samoa, but a certified copy must be maintained at the registered office; bearer shares are prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of activities and economic substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the virtual expense card issuing program precisely, including network membership, sponsor bank arrangements, and licensing references; a bare 'investment holding' description triggers economic substance interrogation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no domestic business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no taxable goods or services are supplied in Samoa and that no Samoan-resident customers are onboarded to the card program.
Confirm the existing AML/CFT program and reporting obligations to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; a card issuer must attach the Central Bank of Samoa special licence reference.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file attracts a late penalty of WST 500; three consecutive defaults cause automatic strike-off from the Register and forfeiture of tax-exemption status. The registered agent must notify the Registrar of director misconduct; failure to do so suspends the agent's licence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 1974, s.38A; however, distributions made by a Samoa International Company are fully exempt from Samoan withholding tax under the International Companies Act 1987, s.199, producing a 0% effective withholding rate on dividends distributed by the IC
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a shareholder of a domestic Samoan company (outside the IC structure) claims treaty relief, the payee must submit a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its home revenue authority to the Samoa Revenue Corporation, complete SRC Form WHT-TRF, and cite the applicable DTA article before the reduced rate is applied at source. Samoa's operative DTA network includes the Samoa-New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (2011). For an exempt IC, no TRC is required: repatriation is effected by (i) board resolution declaring the distribution, (ii) distribution notice from the licensed registered agent, (iii) wire transfer through a licensed Samoan or offshore bank, and (iv) where aggregate distributions exceed WST 1,000,000, a nil WHT return to the SRC evidencing the exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding rates: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest. Under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA, interest and royalties generally remain at 15%. An exempt IC is not a Samoan withholding agent: cross-border royalty and interest payments made by the IC to Mastercard, Visa, or an external lender carry zero Samoan WHT as a matter of the International Companies Act 1987, s.199. For any domestic taxable company, the statutory 15% WHT applies on royalties and interest paid to foreign recipients.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per income year triggers mandatory contemporaneous Local File documentation; Master File documentation is required where the foreign parent group reports consolidated annual revenue exceeding WST 100,000,000 and the Samoan entity exceeds the WST 1,000,000 controlled transaction threshold. These thresholds follow the Samoa Revenue Corporation's practical application of the arm's length standard under the Income Tax Act 1974 (Transfer Pricing Amendment Act 2015).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes. The International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015 and Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations require every International Company to demonstrate substantive economic presence in Samoa. For the virtual card issuer, compliance requires: (i) a licensed registered agent with a physical Samoa office; (ii) a registered office retaining statutory records; (iii) board meetings and material decisions documented in Samoa; (iv) core revenue-generating activities such as programme management, transaction monitoring, and settlement oversight directed from Samoa; and (v) at least two natural-person directors or one licensed corporate director. A card-issuing IC without real substance in Samoa is exposed to deregistration and the loss of the tax-exemption certificate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Exemption Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly supplying false records to the Samoa Revenue Corporation, carrying on domestic business with Samoan residents under the IC tax shield, or filing an annual return that falsely declares derivation of no Samoan-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 1974 ss.120-124 and International Companies Act 1987 s.199(2)-(3): forfeiture of the tax-exemption certificate, full assessment at 27% corporate tax, civil penalties up to 200% of the tax evaded, and a criminal fine not exceeding WST 100,000, with continuing daily fines of WST 20,000 for persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent trading and false declarations; each director is jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties, may be disqualified from acting as a director for up to five years, and faces imprisonment of up to seven years where evasion is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC registration purely as a tax shield while the card-issuing business is actually managed from Hong Kong or mainland China, without registered-agent substance, resident-director authority, or a documented decision-making footprint in Samoa; nominee-only directorship arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations and the Companies Act 2001: deregistration and strike-off by the Registrar, revocation of the International Company licence, and re-assessment of the global card-issuing income as Samoan-resident income at 27% plus 1.5% monthly late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham IC are personally exposed to civil recovery actions by regulators and creditors; departure prohibition orders (travel bans) may be issued during tax recovery proceedings, and custodial sentences of up to five years apply where economic-substance statements are found to be false.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Unlicensed E-Money / Card Issuing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing virtual expense cards, accepting deposit-like prepaid loading, or processing merchant settlement without the approval of the Central Bank of Samoa under the Financial Institutions Act 1996 and the Money-Laundering Prevention Act 2007; weak corporate-client verification and cross-border sanctions-screening failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed financial business is an indictable offence carrying fines up to WST 2,000,000, revocation of any special card-issuing licence, confiscation of the entire processing float, and FIU civil penalties of WST 500,000 for AML compliance failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are held personally accountable for governance failures; courts may disqualify them from corporate management for up to ten years, order personal restitution of customer funds diverted in card settlements, and impose prison sentences of up to seven years for money-laundering facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately processing card payments for sanctioned counterparties, fraudulent merchant onboarding, or knowingly misrepresenting the card programme to Visa and Mastercard through a sponsor-bank arrangement that contradicts the Samoa IC licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act and Samoa's foreign-account-tax-compliance framework: immediate licence suspension, fines of WST 1,000,000 per programme, regulatory repossession of cardholder files, and referral for mutual legal assistance and criminal asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve such acts face extradition-capable money-laundering charges, personal asset forfeiture, and imprisonment for up to ten years; in civil claims, directors are personally liable to cardholders and network operators under wrongful-trading principles without limitation of liability.
